items.name: Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez: over for 2026
items.teaser: The 28th Voiles raced 26 September to 4 October with 253 boats entered; the gulf is back to working boats
items.story: For nine days the Gulf of Saint-Tropez held the year's great gathering of sail: the 28th Voiles de Saint-Tropez ran from 26 September to 4 October 2026, with 253 classic and modern yachts entered, around 50 Maxis among them, three J-Class yachts back in the gulf and the Rolex Trophy marking its twentieth year. The organisers called it a very good edition: the weather allowed every planned race to be sailed, and race director Georges Korhel noted that the TP52s ran away with the fast IRC-0 class. The quays have emptied since. The next edition is listed for late September 2027.
items.why: Too late for this year: look at the 2027 calendar card and book the Saint-Tropez berth early.

items.name: The sea in late October
items.teaser: October water off Hyères and Saint-Tropez averages about 19.5C and falls through the month
items.story: The honest number: the long-run October average for the sea is about 19.4C at Hyères, 19.5C at Saint-Tropez and 19.1C at Toulon, with a spread from roughly 16 to 22C depending on the year and the wind. A mistral turns the surface over and can knock several degrees off in a day; a calm, sunny spell keeps it near 20C. The summer was hot: Saint-Tropez read 28C in the first week of September 2026, against a seasonal norm of 23.1C, so the water started the autumn warm. From Sunday 25 October the clocks go back and the swimming hour after lunch gets shorter.
items.why: Swim at midday after two calm days, never the morning after a mistral; wetsuits for anyone who feels the cold.
facts: Mid-Oct to end Nov, cooling week by week
After a mistral the water can be several degrees colder: wait for calm

items.name: The islands on their winter boats
items.teaser: Porquerolles keeps its boat all year from La Tour Fondue; Port-Cros and Le Levant run reduced, not daily
items.story: The car-free islands do not shut, but they slow right down. TLV runs the crossing to Porquerolles from La Tour Fondue on the Giens peninsula all year round; out of season the Le Lavandou tourist office warns that departures to Port-Cros and Le Levant are not daily and timetables are reduced, so a day on Port-Cros has to be built around the boat. The island tables have closed with the season: the Plage d'Argent and the Mas du Langoustier on Porquerolles both ran until late September. Pack a picnic from the mainland, hire a bike at the port and have the trails nearly to yourself.
items.why: Check the day's return boat before you leave the quay: in winter missing it can mean a night on the island.

items.name: Fêtes de la Châtaigne, Collobrières: 18 and 25 October
items.teaser: Two chestnut Sundays still to come: the international day on 18 Oct, the old trades on the 25th
items.story: Collobrières, deep in the chestnut forest of the Massif des Maures, gives three October Sundays to its harvest. The first, on 11 October, was the Var producers' day, with dishes cooked by a chef. Sunday 18 October is the international day: a parade of delegations from the twinned towns, food brotherhoods, folk groups and Italian flag-throwers. Sunday 25 October is the artisans' day, a festival of old trades run with the Giens 1900 association. Each runs 9am to 6pm, with roasted chestnuts and marrons glacés on sale in the streets and free guided tours of the village through October.
items.why: Arrive before 9am: the village road fills fast and the shuttles from the Parking Ouest are the sane way in.

items.name: Pressing day at the Varages olive mill, 15 November
items.teaser: A free Sunday at La Varageoise: watch the new oil come off the press, taste it, then walk the olive grove
items.story: In November the olive mills of the Var run day and night, and the Provence Verte tourist offices open one of them to visitors. On Sunday 15 November 2026, from 10:30, the Journée oléicole at Varages starts inside the cooperative mill La Varageoise, which presses the harvest of twelve communes, at the height of the season: you watch the olives go through the press and taste the new oil with a guide. The afternoon is a guided walk through the olive grove of the parc de l'Enclos. It is free, but places are booked through the tourist offices.
items.why: Book a place with the Provence Verte et Verdon tourist office and buy the new oil at the mill counter.

items.name: The Aups truffle market reopens in late November
items.teaser: Thursday mornings in Aups, late November to mid-March; the 2026 opening day is not yet announced
items.story: Aups, on the edge of the Verdon, is the black-truffle town of the Haut-Var, and its producers' market for private buyers runs on Thursday mornings from late November to mid-March. Last season opened on Thursday 20 November 2025, the third Thursday of the month, and drew professionals and private buyers from the first morning. If the pattern holds, the 2026 opening would be Thursday 19 November, but no date had been published when checked on 17 October. Local reporting has called recent seasons mixed, so prices and volumes will depend on the autumn rain in the oak woods.
items.why: Go early on a Thursday, look before you buy, and let the producer show you the cut flesh.
facts: Thursday mornings, late Nov–mid-Mar; 2026 opening date not yet announced

items.name: Chestnut menus in Collobrières
items.teaser: Wild boar braised with the village's own chestnuts and ceps, on the plane-shaded square at La Petite Fontaine
items.story: Collobrières does not only sell its chestnuts in October; it cooks them. La Petite Fontaine, on the Place de la République, runs dedicated chestnut menus in autumn, and the dish that sums up the village is the daube de sanglier aux marrons et cèpes: wild boar from the surrounding forest, braised slowly with Collobrières chestnuts and ceps, about 24 euros on its own or inside the three-course menu at about 34 euros. The menu is short because the daube takes two days. Finish across the village at the Confiserie Azuréenne, candying Maures chestnuts since 1948, with a free little museum of the old machines.
items.why: Book lunch on a chestnut Sunday well ahead, or come on a quiet weekday when the square is yours.

items.name: Beaujolais Nouveau, Thursday 19 November
items.teaser: The third Thursday of November: the new Beaujolais goes on sale from midnight, on the Var coast as everywhere
items.story: Since a decree of 29 October 1985, Beaujolais Nouveau may be sold from the third Thursday of November, and in 2026 that is Thursday 19 November. It is not a Var wine, and in Provence it is a bar-counter ritual rather than a feast, but it is the night the wine bars and bistros of Toulon and the coast pour the new gamay and the year's harvest becomes something to drink. For the Var's own answer, wait two weeks: the Bandol growers celebrate their vintage on the port in early December, which is the calendar card worth planning around.
items.why: Drink one glass for the date, then save the evening's money for a bottle of Bandol red.

items.name: Hyères fashion and photography festival, 15–18 October
items.teaser: The 41st Hyères festival is on at the Villa Noailles until Sunday; its exhibitions stay up into 2027
items.story: Since 1986 the Villa Noailles, the modernist house built above Hyères for Charles and Marie-Laure de Noailles, has hosted a festival where young fashion designers, photographers and accessory makers compete before juries from the trade. The 41st edition runs from Thursday 15 to Sunday 18 October 2026, so the final days are this weekend. When the juries leave, the exhibitions stay: the villa's own page says they are open to the public until 28 February 2027, while regional tourism listings give 16 October to 10 January and mark the dates to be confirmed.
items.why: Go this weekend for the festival atmosphere, or any winter afternoon for the shows without the crowd.

items.teaser: Cheval Blanc shut on 11 October; Club 55 is listed open until 1 November; the beach itself never closes
items.story: Saint-Tropez is folding up for the winter. Cheval Blanc St-Tropez, home of La Vague d'Or, was listed open from 7 May to 11 October 2026 and is now closed; no 2027 reopening date had been announced when checked. On Pampelonne the beach clubs set their own seasons: Shellona's ran to 30 September, while Club 55 is listed open daily from 10am to 5pm until Sunday 1 November. The lifeguard post at the boulevard Patch stopped on 4 October. The beach itself stays open every day, free, all year, and in November the long sand is almost empty.

items.name: Dates that change the week
items.teaser: Clocks back on Sunday 25 October, All Saints on Sunday 1 November, and no MICHELIN 2027 date yet
items.story: Three dates shape the next six weeks. On Sunday 25 October, the last Sunday of the month, France moves its clocks back an hour at 3am: the light comes earlier and the evenings close in before dinner. Sunday 1 November is All Saints, Toussaint, a public holiday when families visit the cemeteries with chrysanthemums and the last seasonal businesses close. And the chefs are waiting for the MICHELIN Guide France 2027: no ceremony date or host city had been announced by mid-October. The 2026 ceremony was held in Monaco on 16 March, the 2025 one in Metz on 31 March.
items.why: Reset the boat's clocks on the 25th and plan Pampelonne goodbyes before Toussaint.

items.name: Fête de la Truffe Noire d'Aups
items.teaser: Truffle dogs, a producers' market and Provençal dancing in the Haut-Var's truffle town, late January
items.story: Every January the truffle growers' syndicate of Aups and the Maison de la Truffe et du Verdon put the black truffle in the street for a weekend: a truffle market on the village square, cavage demonstrations with dogs and their handlers, tastings, Provençal dances and fireworks. The 33rd edition ran on 24 and 25 January 2026, with a charity auction for the collegiate church. Entry has been free. The 2027 dates had not been published when checked in October 2026; the festival is usually held in late January, at the height of the melanosporum season.
items.why: Watch a cavage demonstration before you buy: you will understand the price.
facts: Usually late January; 2027 dates not yet published

items.name: Corso Fleuri du Mimosa, Bormes-les-Mimosas
items.teaser: Floats dressed in mimosa through the medieval village in February; one source gives 20–21 February 2027
items.story: Bormes-les-Mimosas has paraded its winter flower for generations: the 82nd Corso Fleuri ran on 16 February 2025, and in 2026 the village held its animations on Saturday 14 February and the parade of flower floats on Sunday 15 February. The floats are dressed in mimosa cut from the Maures hills, which turn yellow in February, and the Sunday ends in a flower battle. For 2027 one travel blog gives 20 and 21 February; the commune had not confirmed it when checked. Do not confuse it with Mandelieu's Fête du Mimosa, listed for 9–14 February 2027.
items.why: Drive the mimosa route from Bormes inland on the Saturday, and take the parade on the Sunday.

items.name: Les Bravades de Saint-Tropez, 16–18 May
items.teaser: Every 16 to 18 May since 1558, musket volleys and a bust of Saint Torpes carried through the streets
items.story: The Bravade is Saint-Tropez's own feast, not a show for visitors: since 1558 the town has honoured Saint Torpes, its patron, every year on 16, 17 and 18 May. The bravadeurs in their uniforms fire blank musket volleys, the saint's bust is carried through the town behind drums and fifes, there is a musketeers' mass and a procession to the Sainte-Anne chapel. The dates never move, whatever the day of the week; in 2027 they fall from Sunday to Tuesday. Access is free. The detailed 2027 programme had not been published when checked.
items.why: Stand back from the musket volleys, and book beds early: the town fills with Tropéziens home for the feast.

items.teaser: Young designers compete at the Villa Noailles each June; the 20th edition ran 25–28 June 2026
items.story: Design Parade is the Villa Noailles' summer twin of its October fashion festival: young designers of objects and interiors show their work and compete for prizes in and around the cubist house that Robert Mallet-Stevens built above Hyères in the 1920s. The 20th edition ran from 25 to 28 June 2026, with its exhibitions open to the public from 29 June to 30 August. The 2027 dates had not been announced when checked; recent editions have fallen in the last week of June.

items.name: Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez 2027
items.teaser: Classic and modern yachts race the gulf at the turn of September and October; 2027 is listed for 26 Sep–4 Oct
items.story: Les Voiles is the end-of-summer meeting of the Mediterranean's sailing yachts: classic wooden boats, J-Class, Maxis and modern racers sharing the gulf for a week of racing from the Société Nautique de Saint-Tropez. It began in 1981 as a challenge between two yachts racing to Club 55, which still gives its name to a cup. The Saint-Tropez tourist office lists the 2027 edition from 26 September to 4 October, daily from 9am to 9pm, free to watch; some of its pages give 25 September to 3 October, so treat the dates as provisional.

items.name: Fêtes de la Châtaigne, Collobrières
items.teaser: Three October Sundays of chestnuts, marrons glacés and parades in the Maures; 2027 dates not yet out
items.story: Collobrières is the chestnut capital of the Massif des Maures, and each October it gives three Sundays to the harvest, each with its own theme. In 2026 they were 11, 18 and 25 October: a producers' day with a chef, an international day with twinned towns and folk groups, and an artisans' day of old trades, each from 9am to 6pm. Entry is free; there is paid parking and a free shuttle from the edge of the village. The 2027 dates were not published when checked; expect three Sundays in October.

items.name: Fête des Vins de Bandol, 5–6 December 2026
items.teaser: The Bandol growers pour their wines on the port on the first weekend of December
items.story: Formerly the Fête du Millésime, the Fête des Vins de Bandol is the appellation's year-end thanksgiving: the estates of Bandol, where Mourvèdre reds must spend at least 18 months in wood, set up on the port to pour their wines and present the year's vintage. The 2026 edition is listed as confirmed for Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 December on the port; the 2025 edition ran on 6 and 7 December. It is the warmest winter day out on the coast, and the place to taste a dozen Bandol estates side by side before choosing which cellar door to drive to.
items.why: Come with a list of two or three estates to compare, and buy at the cellar door afterwards.
facts: Sat 5–Sun 6 Dec 2026 (listed as confirmed); usually the first weekend of December
